name: Question 5
problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{z}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}z{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.$*
worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}z{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,z\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le {x}^{3}}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}z{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/54d8420870ea92e42811a13ed2c4563c5c9ccb674ee8c3b6a277186c0fba21da.png)

The region $D$ is type II region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,z\le x\le 1}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $z=z(x),$ is

$$
x=z\,⟹\,z=x
$$

and the bottom boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
z=0.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region is

$$
D={(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le z\le x},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/7f19b63139a3d38c321e9938c1e8fbbf84e924df51d9b9b057d0151fc269550d.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{z}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}z{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}z{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}[z{\int }_{0}^{{x}^{3}}{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}z[{e}^{y}]_{0}^{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}z({e}^{{x}^{3}}-1)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[({e}^{{x}^{3}}-1){\int }_{0}^{x}z\,\text{d}z]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{{x}^{3}}-1){[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{0}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}({e}^{{x}^{3}}-1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}{e}^{{x}^{3}}-{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{1}{3}{e}^{{x}^{3}}-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[e-1-1+0] \\  & =\frac{e-2}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as ∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫u1(x,z)u2(x,z)zeydydzdx.

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration R can be written as a type III region as follows: R={(x,y,z):0≤z≤1,z≤x≤1,0≤y≤x3}

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to y, the y-limits remain the same as before: ∫ab∫v1(x)v2(x)∫0x3zeydydzdx

Now, we consider the projection D of R onto the xz-plane shown below.

The region D is type II region in the xz-plane: D={(x,z):0≤z≤1,z≤x≤1}.

To change the order of integration from dydxdz to dydzdx, we write D as a type I region.

Notice that the top boundary of the region D, written in the form z=z(x), is x=z⟹z=x and the bottom boundary of the region D is z=0.

Then, the type I representation of the region is D={(x,z):0≤x≤1,0≤z≤x},

as shown in the diagram below.

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain ∫01∫z1∫0x3zeydydxdz=∫01∫0x∫0x3zeydydzdx=∫01∫0x[z∫0x3eydy]dzdx=∫01∫0xz[ey]0x3dzdx=∫01∫0xz(ex3−1)dzdx=∫01[(ex3−1)∫0xzdz]dx=∫01(ex3−1)[12z2]0xdx=∫0112x2(ex3−1)dx=12∫01x2ex3−x2dx=12[13ex3−13x3]01=16[e−1−1+0]=e−26.
